subject: SLA: volume-trigger thresholds & rollover credits
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA: volume-trigger thresholds & rollover credits

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look promising. Before we move forward with a pilot, procurement has asked for clarity on two items in the SLA/addendum you shared:

1) Volume-trigger thresholds: we need to understand how you define a "trigger" (monthly committed units vs. 30-day moving avg) and what evidence you use to decide that a trigger was hit.
2) Rollover credits: if our usage is below commitment one month but above in the next, does Redwood allow rolling credits forward/back? If so, at what rate (100% of unused converted, or partial)?

Our use will be spiky due to marketing events — we expect months at ~40% of commit and occasional spikes at 150% for 2–3 days. Procurement would prefer rollover rather than recurring overage charges.

Can your team propose a structure (simple tiers + rollover treatment) that we can take to legal and procurement? If possible, include an example with numbers.

I'll also attach the procurement redline we expect to send if we get internal approval.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Patel
Head of Cloud Platform, BrightCart
attachments: BRIGHTCART-PO-2026.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA: volume-trigger thresholds & rollover credits

Hi Samira — great question, thanks for the clear context.

Quick answers up front:
- Trigger definition: we propose monthly committed units (billing month) with a 30-day trailing lookback used for smoothing. A "trigger event" is evaluated at month close and is supported by token/embedding invoices + your account's usage report.
- Rollover credits: we can offer a partial rollover mechanism (50% of unused commitment converts to credits applied to overage in the following 2 months). We think a 2-month window balances flexibility with predictable economics.

I've attached a short draft addendum (BC-SLA-Addendum-v0.3.pdf) and a worked example. High-level proposal (for discussion):

Option A — Standard commit (lower discount, no rollover): 100k units/month commit, 8% discount on per-unit price, overage billed at on-demand rate.
Option B — Rollover-friendly (moderate discount + partial rollover): 200k units/month commit, 16% discount, 50% of unused units convert to credits for up to 2 subsequent months, overage beyond credits billed at on-demand.
Option C — High-commit with uplift (highest discount + rollover + priority SLA lane): 500k units/month commit, 24% discount, 75% rollover conversion for 1 month only, includes Priority SLA (1-hour P1 response, 4-hour P2).

Example (Option B): committed 200k units. Month 1 usage: 80k (unused 120k -> 60k rollover credit). Month 2 usage: 260k (200k commit + 60k credit cover -> 0 overage). Month 3 usage: 320k (200k commit + remaining credits 0 -> 120k overage billed at on-demand less discount).

If this direction sounds reasonable, Ben can produce a precise pricing table and Marissa can draft the contract language for the rollover clause. When would your procurement/finance folks be available for a 30-minute sync?

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
attachments: BC-SLA-Addendum-v0.3.pdf, usage-breakdown-worksheet.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA: volume-trigger thresholds & rollover credits

Thanks Hannah — adding a few concrete pricing scenarios so procurement can model cashflow. Notes below assume USD and the per-unit on-demand list price is $0.004 per unit.

Scenario math (monthly):
- Option A (100k commit): effective price = $0.00368 (8% off) -> commit cost = $368; overage billed at $0.004.
- Option B (200k commit, 50% rollover): effective price = $0.00336 (16% off) -> commit cost = $672. Rollover credit: 50% of unused -> credits valued at $0.00336 per credited unit. Credits expire after 2 months.
- Option C (500k commit, priority lane): effective price = $0.00304 (24% off) -> commit cost = $1,520. 75% rollover for 1 month; priority SLA adds an uplift of $0.00012/unit effective to the committed price.

Commercial considerations we recommend including in contract:
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-up with pro-rata settlement for sustained overages (>120% of commit for 2 consecutive months).
- Burst capacity: a capped burst pool (up to 150% of commit for 72 hours) at a reduced overage rate to avoid surprise bills during one-off events.
- Rollover accounting: credits should be treated as invoice line items with clear expiration dates and reporting.

I've put a sample pricing table in the worksheet. Marissa — flag anything that needs legal nuance before we send to BrightCart procurement.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Economics, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCart DevOps <ops@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA: volume-trigger thresholds & rollover credits

Hannah / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the worked example. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance after looking at the numbers:

1) Rollover rate: procurement is pushing for a 100% rollover conversion for at least the first month (they argue that our usage model is lumpy and credits should map 1:1 for the immediate following month). Can you do 100% for Month+1 and 50% for Month+2 as a concession?
2) Burst pool: we like the capped burst pool idea but would prefer it to be a paid option (one-time monthly buffer add-on) rather than variable overage billing for psychological reasons. Can you give a fixed monthly buffer SKU (e.g., +20% buffer at discounted rate)?
3) SLA uplift specifics: priority SLA (1-hour P1) is mission-critical for us; what exactly is included in the Priority SLA lane (on-call rotation, escalation path, dedicated Slack channel?) and what operational hours apply (24x7 or business hours)?

We're keen to get a pilot started but need procurement to feel comfortable the economics won't spike BOM. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow morning PT if you can.

Regards,
Samira

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@brightcart.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA: volume-trigger thresholds & rollover credits

Samira — appreciate the clarity from procurement. We discussed internally and can offer the following compromise that aims to address procurement's concerns while keeping our unit economics predictable:

Final negotiated proposal (summary):
- Commit tiers: 100k / 250k / 500k units per month. (We replaced 200k with 250k to smooth pricing bands.)
- Rollover credits: Month+1 = 100% of unused units converted to credits; Month+2 = 50% conversion, credits usable for invoice offset only, expire after Month+2.
- Fixed burst SKU: Optional buffer SKU priced at 20% of commit for the month, billed monthly if purchased; buffer covers bursts up to +20% for 72 hours each month at a 50% discounted overage rate.
- Priority SLA lane: 1-hour P1 response, 4-hour P2, 24x7 coverage for P1. Includes a named escalation roster, direct Slack channel (monitored 24x7 for P1), and monthly operational review. Priority lane is included for the 500k tier or as an add-on for lower tiers for an uplift fee.
- True-up: quarterly true-up with pro-rata invoices for sustained overages (>125% of commit for 2 months).

Next steps:
1) I've updated the addendum to reflect these points (BC-SLA-Addendum-v0.3 -> BC-SLA-Addendum-v0.4).
2) If that looks good, I'll send the DocuSign for signature and Ben will issue the final pricing table.
3) Please confirm if procurement wants the fixed buffer SKU added to the initial purchase, and provide names for the operational contact who will be on the priority Slack if we enable the lane.
